# Golden fixtures: SYNTHETIC datasets

**Every file in this folder is synthetic.** It was generated by `generate.ts` (or, for two
`expected-results.json` files, computed by hand) and contains **no real taxpayer data**. No client
file was read, copied or anonymised to make it.

- Names are all "Sample ..." (Sample Traders 01, Sample Client Textiles 01, Sample Rice Mills 03,
  Sample Deductor Industries 04 and so on). No real company names.
- PANs follow the reserved-looking pattern `ZZZ<type>S####Z` (for example `ZZZFS0001Z`).
  GSTINs are `<state><PAN>1Z<check>`, and the check character is computed with the repo's own
  `calculateGstinChecksum` (`packages/tax-engine/src/validators/gstin.ts`), so every GSTIN passes
  `validateGstin` while being obviously fake.
- TAN `ZZZS90001Z`, BSR codes `999000x`, tokens `99000...`, CPINs `2511039900000x`, emails on
  `example.invalid`, bank "Sample Bank Ltd".

These stand in for item 15 of the founder checklist (5 real anonymised datasets from Amritsar CA
firms) so the pipelines can be tested now. The real files drop in beside them, see below.

## Run

```
npm run test:golden
# or one dataset
npx tsx --test tests/golden-fixtures/synthetic/a-messy-purchase-register.test.ts
```

Regenerate the generated files (deterministic, fixed seed):

```
npx tsx tests/golden-fixtures/synthetic/generate.ts
```

`b-qrmp-client-pack/expected-results.json` and `c-rcm-rule42-43/expected-results.json` are
hand-computed and are not touched by the generator.

The tests import source files directly (tax engine, queue-worker recon, the ingestion CSV parser and
two API route modules) so no build is needed. No package's own `test` script picks up `tests/`,
hence the root `test:golden` script.

Tests named `F<n> ...` are `todo` tests: they assert what the correct behaviour should be, fail
today because of the finding of the same number below, and do not fail the run. When a finding is
fixed, its todo test starts passing and the `todo` marker should be removed.

## Real-dataset slots (gitignored)

`tests/golden-fixtures/real/` is in `.gitignore`. The team fills one folder per slot with the same
file names as the synthetic folder, plus an `expected-results.json` written by the CA who knows the
data. Each test file runs the real slot automatically when `real/<slot>/expected-results.json`
exists (`fixture-support.ts`, `datasets()`), and skips the synthetic-only `F<n>` probes for it.

| Slot | Synthetic stand-in | Real files expected |
|---|---|---|
| `real/a` | `a-messy-purchase-register/` | `purchase-register-nov-2025.csv` (or rename `register.file` in expected-results), `gstr2b-112025.json` (portal download), `expected-results.json` |
| `real/b` | `b-qrmp-client-pack/` | `client.json`, `months.json`, `pmt06-challans.csv`, `expected-results.json` |
| `real/c` | `c-rcm-rule42-43/` | `client.json`, `purchase-register-nov-2025.csv`, `capital-goods-register.csv`, `expected-results.json` |
| `real/d` | `d-traces-conso/` | the TRACES `.conso` file named in `expected-results.json` `file`, `expected-results.json` |
| `real/e` | `e-itns-281n-challan/` | `challan-281n.json`, `book-challans.json`, `challan-list.csv`, `<TAN>.csi`, `expected-results.json` |

Real data must be anonymised before it lands there, and must never be committed.

## The datasets

### (a) messy purchase register + GSTR-2B

- `purchase-register-nov-2025.csv`: 429 lines in a Tally/Busy "Purchase Register" export shape.
  381 data lines (375 invoices plus 6 duplicate postings) from 36 suppliers, with title rows, a
  merged "Tax Amount" header row, blank lines, Busy style "Round Off" ledger rows, two page breaks
  ("Carried Forward", repeated title, "Brought Forward", repeated header) and a "Grand Total".
  GSTINs with spaces, lower case or padding; invoice numbers like `SALES/25-26/1`, `GST/2025-26/007`,
  `BL/00012`; dates as `05-Nov-25`, `05/11/2025`, `2025-11-05`, `5.11.25`, `05-11-2025` and Excel
  serials (`45966`); amounts with Indian digit grouping in quoted cells. Written as `.csv` only:
  no package in the repo depends on `exceljs` or `xlsx`.
- `gstr2b-112025.json`: GSTN GSTR-2B download layout (`data.docdata.b2b[].inv[]` with `inum`, `dt`
  as DD-MM-YYYY, `txval`, `igst`, `cgst`, `sgst`, `cess`, `itcavl`; `data.docdata.cdnr[].nt[]`).
  The repo has no parser for this layout (F12), so the field set follows the public portal
  download and should be checked against the first real file in `real/a`.
- `expected-results.json`: for every register line, which pass of
  `GstReconciliationEngine.reconcile` should pair it with which 2B document, plus the skipped and
  duplicate lines and the summary totals. These follow the matcher's actual logic (pass 1 exact,
  pass 2 normalised number within Rs 1.00, pass 3 normalised number any value), so the scenario
  legend inside the file also says where that logic is questionable.

Result: 305 exact, 39 fuzzy, 15 value mismatch, 16 purchase not in 2B, 13 2B not in register.
The engine agrees with every expectation.

`fixture-support.ts` holds the test-side readers. Because the repo cannot read either file as-is,
these rules stand in for a production importer: header is the first row with a `GSTIN/UIN` cell;
a data row has a GSTIN and a supplier invoice number, everything else is named and skipped;
GSTIN whitespace removed and upper-cased; Indian grouping stripped from amounts; a later row with
the same GSTIN, invoice number, date and taxable value is a duplicate and is dropped.

### (b) QRMP client pack

Q3 FY 2025-26 for a Punjab QRMP client: per-month outward tax and 2B credit, two PMT-06
self-assessment challans (October 52,200; November 27,900), and the quarterly GSTR-3B with
45,800 paid in cash on filing. Tests: IFF, GSTR-1 and 3B due dates (`gstDueDate`), PMT-06 amounts
equal to `GstItcSetOffEngine` cash for each month, the quarter's set-off less PMT-06 by head, and
`gstr3bYear` with cadence QRMP.

### (c) RCM and Rule 42/43 (rice sheller)

November 2025 for a rice sheller selling pre-packaged rice (5 percent, taxable) and loose rice
(exempt), E/F = 0.7. Purchases include RCM on GTA (intra and inter-state), advocate fees, security
services and godown rent from an unregistered landlord, with self-invoice numbers; inputs used only
for taxable, only for exempt, common, non-business and 17(5) blocked; a capital goods register
(common dryer, new common sorter, blocked car). `expected-results.json` has the full Rule 42
(T, T1 to T4, C1, C2, D1, D2, C3) and Rule 43 (Tm, Tr, Te) working, the GSTR-3B 4A/4B/4C figures,
the set-off and GSTR-9 tables 6 and 7.

### (d) TRACES consolidated file

`ZZZS90001Z_140_Q1_202627.conso`: Form 140, Q1 Tax Year 2026-27, FH/BH/CD/DD caret-delimited
records with exactly 18/72/30/45 fields, the positions `parseConsoFile`
(`packages/tax-engine/src/tds/correction.ts:292`) reads, 3 challans and 26 payee rows (one
`PANNOTAVBL` at 20 percent). Tests parse it, check every field, and run `correctionTypesNeeded`
(C3 for replacing PANNOTAVBL, C5 for a PAN change) and `writeCorrection`.

### (e) ITNS 281N challan + CSI

`challan-281n.json` is a request body for `POST /:tanId/challans`
(`apps/api/src/modules/tds/challans.routes.ts`), multi-section as the 2025 Act allows, and is the
same challan as record 1 of the conso. `challan-list.csv` is read by `parseChallanList`.
`ZZZS90001Z.csi` uses an assumed layout
(`DDMMYYYY^BSR^SERIAL^AMOUNT^MAJOR_HEAD^MINOR_HEAD^TAN^BANK`) because the repo has no CSI file
parser (F13); only the upload validator sniffs it. The CSI matching runs through the real
`POST /csi-match` route via Fastify `inject`.

## Findings

Disagreements between what the code does and what these datasets say it should do. The tax engine
was not changed. Each `F<n>` with a todo test fails today as described.

| # | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | `packages/ingestion/src/excel/excel-csv-parser.ts:94`, `:116`, `:46` | `parseInvoiceCsv` takes the first non-blank line as the header, splits cells on every comma (quoted `"1,23,456.00"` breaks), and `normalizeDate` does not read `05-Nov-25`, `5.11.25` or Excel serials. On the raw export it returns 0 valid rows of 381. It has no notion of title, total, round-off or repeated header rows, or duplicates. **Fixed 26 Nov 2026: importer finds the header row, reads quoted cells, Tally/Excel dates and Indian amounts, skips title/total/round-off rows and flags duplicates (PURCHASE mode keeps Rule 46 and place-of-supply as warnings).** |
| F2 | `workers/queue-worker/src/recon/reconciliationEngine.ts:113-114` | Pass 1 compares taxable value and total tax only. An invoice booked as IGST that the supplier reported as CGST+SGST (wrong place of supply) is an EXACT_MATCH with confidence 1.0, although its note says "tax split". 3 cases in (a). **Fixed: every tax head must agree; a head-only difference is MISMATCH_VALUE with a place-of-supply note.** |
| F3 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:217-222` | `itcAvailable` is never read. A 2B line with `itcavl = N` is matched and its tax counted in `totalMatchedItc`. **Fixed: itcavl N goes to totalItcNotAvailable, not totalMatchedItc.** |
| F4 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:134-163` | Pass 2 has no date check at all. A 2B document dated a month earlier with the same normalised number is a FUZZY_MATCH at 0.95. **Fixed: same date 0.95, same month 0.90, another month PROBABLE_MATCH 0.75 (tax at risk).** |
| F5 | `workers/queue-worker/src/jobs/invoiceNormalizerJob.ts:42` | Segments are joined with no separator, so `A/1/12` and `A/11/2` both become `A112`. With values within Rs 1.00, pass 2 pairs them crosswise (first 2B candidate wins). **Fixed: a strict key with segment boundaries is tried before the loose key.** |
| F6 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:169-177` | Pass 3 does not check `docType` (pass 2 does, line 139). An INV in the register and a debit note in 2B cdnr with the same number are reported as MISMATCH_VALUE with a 0.00 difference. **Fixed: pass 3 checks docType; a type clash is MISMATCH_DOCTYPE.** |
| F7 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:86-87` | `period` is only echoed in the report. Register rows dated outside the period (an October late booking, a December invoice keyed into November) are plain PURCHASE_NOT_IN_2B, with no out-of-period flag; reconciling with any other period gives the same result. **Fixed: rows dated after the period are set aside (outOfPeriodPurchase, totalDeferredItc).** |
| F8 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:217-227` | Tax on MISMATCH_VALUE pairs is in neither `totalMatchedItc` nor `totalAtRiskItc`, so 15 invoices' credit vanishes from the totals in (a). **Fixed: every register row lands in exactly one bucket (matched, not available, at risk, deferred).** |
| F9 | `packages/tax-engine/src/gst/gstr3bYear.ts:63` | For QRMP, GSTR-1 and 2B figures are summed over the quarter but `cashPaid` comes from the quarter-end row only, so PMT-06 deposits made in months 1 and 2 (80,100 in (b)) drop out of the quarter and the year totals (45,800 shown, 125,900 paid). |
| F10 | `packages/tax-engine/src/compliance/calendar.ts:48`, `:63` | No PMT-06 type (due the 25th of the next month) and no fixed-sum (35 percent) computation. An unknown type silently falls through to the GSTR-3B rule and returns the 24th. |
| F11 | `apps/api/src/routes/tds.routes.ts:477`, `:482` | `/csi-match` keys challans on BSR + serial + amount without the deposit date. Serials restart per branch per day, so two monthly challans of the same amount at the same branch collide: the second CSI row overwrites the first in the map and a deposited challan is reported unmatched (BOOK-2 in (e)). |
| F12 | `reconciliationEngine.ts:19`, `packages/gsp-adapter/src/types.ts:62` | No parser for the GSTN GSTR-2B JSON download anywhere in the repo. The engine and the GSP adapter only take an already-flattened `Gstr2BRecord` / `Gstr2bInvoiceItem`. The test uses `fixture-support.ts` `load2b`. **Fixed: packages/ingestion/src/gst/gstr2b-json-parser.ts reads b2b, cdnr, b2ba, cdnra.** |
| F13 | `apps/api/src/routes/tds.routes.ts:37`, `apps/api/src/modules/tds/challans.routes.ts:34` | No CSI file parser: both CSI routes take JSON records. The upload validator (`apps/api/src/security/fileUploadValidator.ts:115-117`) only sniffs a caret or a leading TAN/8-digit date. The `.csi` layout here is therefore unverified. |
| F14 | `apps/api/src/routes/tds.routes.ts:477` vs `apps/api/src/modules/tds/challans.routes.ts:214-224` | The two CSI matchers disagree: one pads the serial to 5 digits, ignores the date and needs the exact amount; the other compares the serial as stored (unpadded), requires the date and allows Rs 0.05. The same file can match differently depending on the screen used. (Not covered by a test: the second route needs a database.) |
| F15 | `packages/tax-engine/src/gst/gstr9Engine.ts:286-293` | Table 6 splits the whole 3B ITC (6A) 70/15/15 into inputs, capital goods and services, then adds RCM, imports and ISD on top. RCM credit is already inside 6A, so 6I exceeds 6A by the RCM amount (CGST 146,750 vs 128,150 in (c)). The fixed 70/15/15 split is also not derived from data. |
| F16 | `gstr9Engine.ts:42-43` | No Rule 42/43 calculator. Reversals are accepted only as inputs to GSTR-9 table 7. (c)'s working is by hand; the test checks it against the register, not against product code. |
| F17 | `apps/api/src/modules/gst/recon.routes.ts:23` vs `reconciliationEngine.ts:16`, `apps/api/src/routes/recon.routes.ts:33` | The import schema allows `itcEligibility = INELIGIBLE_RULE_42_43`; the engine type and the `/recon/run` schema do not, so a Rule 42/43 tagged purchase cannot be sent to the matcher. **Fixed: engine type and /recon/run schema accept INELIGIBLE_RULE_42_43.** |
| F18 | `apps/api/src/modules/gst/recon.routes.ts:315-345` | The database recon route (a second, separate matcher) has a pass 3 that can never run: its condition is identical to pass 2, and pass 2 has no value tolerance, so value mismatches are stored as FUZZY_MATCH. Not exercised here (needs a database). **Fixed: the database route now calls the shared matcher and stores VENDOR_NOT_IN_2B for rows not in 2B (migration 0041 allows the new statuses). Covered by the API test "a raw Tally purchase register and the GSTR-2B download are uploaded and reconciled in the database".** |

None of these were fixed.
